about: The figures docs/plans/judge-v6.md cites, recomputed from the records of the claim judge's first round by scripts/judge_v6_figures.py. Nothing was judged anew: every figure re-reads the round's saved replies with the claim judge's own code, and v2's two extra passes are replayed from the call cache with no call to the API.

a_tuning_set_split.scope: The 125 tuning answers as the pass files record them, under v5's named list and v6's (v5's plus the five added cases). The kept set is the named answers labeled supported that v2's stored verdict passes; for each, how many of revision 1's three passes pass it at each cell of the grid under test and at t = 70 with s off.

b_v2_three_passes.scope: v2's three passes on the 125 tuning answers: its stored verdicts (salt judge, from the pass files' v2_passed) and its two extra passes of the choice step (salts judge-s2 and judge-s3), replayed from the call cache. Errors per pass and summed on both splits. The totals on v5's split are asserted equal to stage-a-choice.json's v2 entry.

c_rev1_errors.scope: Revision 1's three passes. Per pass and summed: false passes and false fails on the 93 and the 32 at every cell of the grid under test and at t = 70 with s off, where the 106 and the 19 are read too. The four answers behind v5's stop: their verdict at t = 70 with s off and their weakest claim under each salt. The own-name check: the verdicts at t = 70 with s off that move when a flag on the name Bedrock inside words of no claim is ignored, on docs-ai-003-p3 (the champion's run) and on any of the 375 judgings.

d_scores.scope: Revision 1's 375 judgings (125 answers under three salts). Claim scores: every claim's score in the band 50 to 85, the share of them that are multiples of 5, and the off-level values. Weakest claims: judgings whose lowest claim score is 65, 70, 72 or 75, and at 70 by label outside each named list. The sweep: totals over the three passes of false passes and false fails at every whole t from 50 to 90 with s off, on the 106 and on the 93.

e_skeptic.scope: Revision 1's 375 judgings. The search's confidence on every false pass at t = 70 with s off outside v5's named cases; the highest confidence on a judging of an answer labeled supported that passes at t = 70 with s off, over all 125 answers and outside each named list. The s sweep at t = 70 on the 106 and the 93: totals over the three passes, with the false passes removed and the false fails added against s off. Verdicts that s = 70 and s = 90 change against s off, over the 375 judgings, at t = 70 and at t = 50.

g_events_and_cost.scope: Every distinct judging of the round: the pilot's 60 (20 answers under three salts), the first draft's 125 (its salt judge repeats the pilot's on those 20, the same cached replies) and revision 1's 375. Retries, judge errors, dropped support entries with the span check's reasons, searches naming words not in the answer, and the verdicts that fail only because of a dropped entry, at every cell of v5's grid and of the grid under test. Cost per answer and the output-token share per pass, from the pass files' usage at configs/judge-v5.yaml's pricing; v2's cost per answer from the ledger's choice entry less revision 1's two extra passes, and from its replayed replies' usage at configs/default.yaml's pricing.

h_fail_rates.scope: The 125 tuning answers: the answers v2's stored verdict passes and its fail rate; revision 1's passes and fail rate under each salt at each grid t, and at t = 70, with s off and with s = 49.

i_build_check_fitted.scope: The 32 named answers under v6's list, over three passes at t = 70 with s off. Revision 1's errors (judge errors would count, there are none), the errors the proposal's changes would remove on the answers they were written from, and the difference, labeled fitted: a projection on the passes the changes were fitted to, not evidence. Beside it, v2's errors on the same 32 over its stored pass and its two replayed passes.
i_build_check_fitted.label: fitted

j_reason_rules.scope: Revision 1's 375 judgings at t=70 s=off, with the first reader's classes of the judge's reasons from classes.json (the second reader's classes on batch 1 are not read). Each rule is a verdict per judging, built from the saved scores, the base verdict and the saved classes, nothing judged anew. Per pass and summed: false passes and false fails on the 106 outside v5's named cases, the 93 outside v6's, the 19 v5 names and the 32 v6 names, beside revision 1's totals at the same cell, with every judging whose verdict a rule moves against revision 1's and the classified claims it turned on (claim: the index in the judging's claim table, from 0, as classes.json numbers it). Then the claims of batches 2 and 3 by class, checked against the file's own summary.

class_legend.RW: plain rewording, arithmetic or a unit conversion of what a quote states
class_legend.EXT: an implication or extension beyond the quote
class_legend.NAME: a name or term in no quote
class_legend.QUAL: a qualifier or scope beyond the quote
class_legend.OTHER: another gap, with its kind: a headerless table cell, or a claim that depends on the current date

two_type_rule.rule: At t=70 s=off, a judging fails when revision 1 fails it (Assessment.verdict at that cell, the base verdict, flagged items included), or when any classified claim of that judging, in any of the three batches, has the first reader's class NAME (a name or term in no quote) or OTHER of the kind 'a headerless table cell'. Every other judging passes; a claim that was not classified is read as the base verdict reads it.

categories_only.rule: At t=70 s=off, the classes alone decide: a judging passes only when every claim tied at its lowest score has the first reader's class ST or RW (stated outright, or a plain rewording, arithmetic or a unit conversion of what a quote states); any other class at the lowest score fails it. A judging whose lowest score is above 85 counts as passing and one whose lowest score is below 50 as failing, since those claims were not classified. The base verdict's other parts (flagged items, the search, dropped support entries) are not read.
